result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: addGuests.handler.ts contains `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — `err` is never logged and execution continues to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, so the client shows a success toast even when all guest emails fail. Guests are persisted via `prisma.booking.update` before this, so the notification failure is silently swallowed and undetectable. This is a real defect (silent failure + misleading success) introduced by the diff, though email delivery is best-effort in many systems, so confidence is moderate.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This means email failures are intentionally swallowed (and `err` isn’t logged), reducing observability and making notification failures hard to detect, even though the core mutation (persisting guests) succeeds.
